precepts.text: Heathens from Babylon and Cuthah were planted in Samaria, and each nation made its own gods in the high places the Samaritans had made.
precepts.point: Shalmaneser besieged Samaria for three years and carried Israel to Halah, Habor and the cities of the Medes. The scattered tribes moved further east, into Iran, Russia, China and Japan.

note.label: The Dividing Hatred: Cornelius the Centurion

precepts.why:
“In the twelfth year of Ahaz king of Judah began Hoshea the son of Elah to reign in Samaria over Israel nine years”. Ahaz, wicked and weak, was over Judah, and Hoshea was over Ephraim, the northern kingdom. Hoshea “did that which was evil in the sight of the Lord, but not as the kings of Israel that were before him”.

“Against him came up Shalmaneser king of Assyria”. This is Pul’s son. In 1 Chronicles 5 it was Pul, Tiglath-pileser, who came first and took Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh; now his son Shalmaneser comes and does the most. The northern kingdom was not taken all at once. It was done in waves: one group taken out here, some of Reuben, some of Asher there, until almost all of Ephraim was out of the land.

Hoshea became his servant and paid him, then conspired against him: “he had sent messengers to So king of Egypt, and brought no present to the king of Assyria”. He tried to align himself with Egypt to defy Assyria, so the king of Assyria bound him in prison, “went up to Samaria, and besieged it three years”, and “carried Israel away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes”. That is modern day Iran, bordering Russia. From there our people kept migrating further and further east: the northern kingdom became Scythians, moving from Iran into Russia, some as far as China, some as far as Japan, where they became samurai.

Why it happened: “the children of Israel had sinned against the Lord their God”, and they “did secretly those things that were not right”. They thought God wasn’t watching; he saw it all. They built high places in every city, “rejected his statutes, and his covenant”, “followed vanity, and became vain, and went after the heathen”. So “the Lord was very angry with Israel, and removed them out of his sight: there was none left but the tribe of Judah only”. Yet “Judah kept not the commandments” either, and “the Lord rejected all the seed of Israel”. God was done with all twelve: the northern kingdom into captivity, and Judah next.

Then the land was filled with heathen: “the king of Assyria brought men from Babylon, and from Cuthah, and from Ava, and from Hamath, and from Sepharvaim, and placed them in the cities of Samaria instead of the children of Israel”. The Lord sent lions to kill them for their evil, so a priest was brought back to teach them “the manner of the God of the land”, how to sacrifice so they could stay in the land in Ephraim’s absence. “Howbeit every nation made gods of their own, and put them in the houses of the high places which the Samaritans had made”. The northern kingdom was called Samaritans because Samaria was their capital, and these heathen sacrificed in the very high places Ephraim made for their idols. And “the men of Babylon made Succoth–benoth, and the men of Cuth made Nergal, and the men of Hamath made Ashima”.

So the carrying away in 1 Chronicles 5:26 was the start of this: God himself stirred up the kings of Assyria against the tribes that went whoring after other gods, and the northern kingdom was broken and scattered, with strangers set in their place.

precepts.text: Reuben was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph.
precepts.point: The judgment followed him: forasmuch as he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph, and the genealogy is not reckoned after the birthright. The firstborn lost the birthright over it.

note.label: Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel

precepts.why:
“Now the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel, (for he was the firstborn; but, forasmuch as he defiled his father’s bed, his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph the son of Israel: and the genealogy is not to be reckoned after the birthright.”

The judgment followed Reuben. Israel heard that he lay with Bilhah, and forasmuch as he defiled his father's bed, his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph; the genealogy is not reckoned after the birthright. The firstborn lost the birthright over it.

precepts.text: Reuben's birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph because he defiled his father's bed.
precepts.point: Thou shalt not excel: Reuben would not excel as the firstborn, because he went up to his father's couch. His birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph because he defiled his father's bed, and the genealogy is not to be reckoned after the birthright.

note.label: Genesis 49: What Shall Befall the Twelve Tribes in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“Now the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel, (for he was the firstborn; but, forasmuch as he defiled his father’s bed, his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph the son of Israel: and the genealogy is not to be reckoned after the birthright.” Reuben was the firstborn, the beginning of his father’s strength, and the excellency of dignity and the excellency of power belonged to him. But he went up to his father’s couch and defiled his father’s bed, and his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph.

That is “thou shalt not excel.” Reuben, the so-called Seminole Indian today, would not excel as the firstborn; the genealogy is not reckoned after the birthright. The Seminoles were great warriors, and unstable as water, nomads always moving around, as the scripture said.

precepts.text: Reuben was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph; the birthright shows why the firstborn and the inheritance mattered so much in Israel.
precepts.point: Behind the words the wife of the dead stands the law of the husband's brother: if brethren dwell together and one dies having no child, his brother takes the widow to wife, and the firstborn she bears succeeds in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. That first child is basically the dead brother's child; he gets the rights of inheritance as if the brother were still alive, so the brother's name stays in the earth and his house is built up.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
“Now the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel, (for he was the firstborn; but, forasmuch as he defiled his father’s bed, his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph the son of Israel: and the genealogy is not to be reckoned after the birthright.”

Reuben was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph. The birthright shows why the firstborn and the inheritance mattered so much in Israel, and why the law took such care that a dead brother's name and inheritance were raised up.

precepts.text: Reuben was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph; the birthright shows why the firstborn and the inheritance mattered so much in Israel.
precepts.point: What law is that going back to? That law goes back to Deuteronomy 25, the duty of the husband's brother: the widow of the dead does not marry without unto a stranger, and the firstborn she bears succeeds in the name of the dead brother, that his name be not put out of Israel. This law was taught in full when it was read ahead at Ruth 1:6-9 in these notes: the firstborn carries the weight of the name, and the shoe was loosed from him that would not build up his brother's house.

note.label: Ruth 4: Boaz Redeems the Inheritance

precepts.why:
“Now the sons of Reuben the firstborn of Israel, (for he was the firstborn; but, forasmuch as he defiled his father’s bed, his birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph the son of Israel: and the genealogy is not to be reckoned after the birthright.”

Reuben was the firstborn, but because he defiled his father's bed his birthright was given to the sons of Joseph. The birthright shows why the firstborn and the inheritance mattered so much in Israel. That is why Boaz would not let the field pass without the wife of the dead: the name of the dead had to be raised up upon his inheritance.

precepts.text: When the Most High is against a people, their ox is slain before their eyes and their ass is violently taken away.
precepts.point: They took away much cattle and a hundred thousand captives, for the war was of the Most High; this is the curse of Deuteronomy 28 falling on the enemy instead of on us.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 5: The Tribes East of Jordan and Their Captivity

precepts.why:
“Thine ox shall be slain before thine eyes, and thou shalt not eat thereof: thine ass shall be violently taken away from before thy face, and shall not be restored to thee: thy sheep shall be given unto thine enemies, and thou shalt have none to rescue them.” When the Most High is against a people, this is what happens to them.

Here the curse of Deuteronomy 28 falls on the enemy instead of on us. Reuben, Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh made war with the Hagarites, “And they were helped against them”, “for they cried to God in the battle, and he was intreated of them; because they put their trust in him.” “And they took away their cattle; of their camels fifty thousand, and of sheep two hundred and fifty thousand, and of asses two thousand, and of men an hundred thousand.” “For there fell down many slain, because the war was of God.”

precepts.text: The children of Israel are commanded to make fringes in the borders of their garments to remember and do the commandments.
precepts.point: Because of this the Most High stirred up the spirit of Pul, that is Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, who carried Reuben, Gad, and the half tribe of Manasseh into captivity unto this day.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 5: The Tribes East of Jordan and Their Captivity

precepts.why:
“Speak unto the children of Israel, and bid them that they make them fringes in the borders of their garments throughout their generations, and that they put upon the fringe of the borders a ribband of blue”. The fringes were given so that we would look upon them and remember the commandments, and do them, and not go a-whoring after our own eyes.

These tribes failed to do that. “And they transgressed against the God of their fathers, and went a whoring after the gods of the people of the land, whom God destroyed before them.” Because of this the Most High stirred up the spirit of Pul, that is Tilgath-pilneser king of Assyria, and he carried away Reuben, Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh into captivity “unto this day.”
